main_text.p: antea uocatus, Senis, cum Romae non liceret per[?] tumultum, Hildebrandi astutia, sine Cæsaris consensu pontifex creabatur. Hic peracta aduersus Benedictum, Sutrensi synodo, Romam illinc uenientes, apud Lateranum aliud concilium conuocauit: in quo hanc legem tulit, ut non apostolicus, sed apostaticus censeretur, qui sedem Petri, Satanae potius, obtineret, uel pecunia uel fauore, uide artem Hildebrandi, sine unanimi consensu Cardinalium. Dediq; potestatem Cardinalibus, clericis ac laicis, talem pontificem anathemate ferire, & quoties loco, si Romae non liceret, synodum aduersus illum conuocare, ac sede propellere. In eo etiam concilio Berengarius Andegauensis archidiaconus, opinionem suam de Eucharistia, coactus est reuocare. In qua affeuerabat, Christum non esse in pane & uino naturaliter, sed sacramentaliter, & tanquam in ministerio, signo, figura aut sacramento. Romanæ terræ capitaneos Nicolaus iste constituit: & Robertum Guiscardum, iuratum mancipium (quod Imperatoris erat) Apuliæ, Calabriæ ac Siciliæ ducem decernebat, uexilloque donabat propter initum cum eo fœdus. Sic fur furem, & latro latronem iuuabat iuxta ueterem Rom. pontificum morem. De fictis[?] diris, dolis, mendaciis, infanis, & arrogantiis, quibus in suarum

page.notes: Printed page number "192" at top left, with a stylised final 2. Running head reads "DE ROM. PONTIFICVM". "per" in "per tumultum" is printed with a ligature-like mark and is doubtful. "Dediq;" is an abbreviation as printed and may stand for "Dedit quoque". "fictis" is read from a worn form "fi&is". The paragraph is continuous across the page with no indent, so it is treated as a continuation. The word "fuarum" at the foot right is the catchword for the next page.
